headline: US Adds 165,000 Jobs in October as Unemployment Falls to 4.1%
summary: The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, beating forecasts, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, signaling renewed labor market strength.
why: U.S. employment data is a primary indicator for economic health and heavily influences Federal Reserve monetary policy decisions regarding interest rates.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Stronger-than-expected job growth points to economic resilience, influencing equities and rate expectations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected nonfarm payrolls and a falling unemployment rate increased expectations for economic strength and potential Federal Reserve rate hikes.
